Dr. Daniel Pompa told Kevin Trudeau about the Drash study out of Germany: an autopsy study that found the number of silver fillings in a mother's mouth was directly tied to how much mercury turned up in her baby's brain.

He says those same fillings never stop leaching. The mercury vapor crosses the blood-brain barrier for as long as the filling stays in your mouth.

Most countries have put limits on these fillings. The US still hasn't.

Kevin Trudeau's take: this is information worth asking your own dentist about.

Dr. Daniel Pompa told Kevin Trudeau where ordinary aluminum exposure actually comes from. It's added to jet fuel, and acid rain carries it down into our food and water supply.

Wrapping hot, fatty food in aluminum foil lets it leach straight into your meal. His advice: keep foil off your food entirely.

He says most deodorants and antiperspirants still carry aluminum too, and your skin absorbs it straight into your body.

Two easy swaps: ditch the foil, and check your deodorant label. Would you make that swap today?

One easy valve to shut off: plastic. A new study he points to found a teaspoon of plastic showing up in autopsies of people's brains.

His simple swap: drink out of glass or steel instead of plastic, every chance you get. What's one plastic habit you could swap out this week?

Dr. Daniel Pompa told Kevin Trudeau seed oils were sold to us as the heart-healthy choice: canola, vegetable and the rest.

His view: that was bad information. The fats our grandparents used, like lard, tallow and butter, held up fine. The seed oils replacing them turn rancid fast and drive inflammation in your cells.

His simple swap: go back to grass-fed butter, tallow or lard for cooking, and read the ingredient list on anything processed.

What's in your kitchen oil right now?
